title: Full-Order Sampling-Based MPC for Torque-Level Locomotion Control via Diffusion-Style Annealing
overview: DIAL-MPC refines sampled actions online using diffusion-inspired annealing. It does not train a diffusion policy.
achievement: Go2 hardware performs sequential jumping with a 7 kg payload. Appendix setup uses 50 Hz planning and 200 Hz low-level commands.
gap: Fast parallel simulation and a short planning horizon constrain the approach. Desktop computation and motion capture limit claims about autonomous field deployment.
setting: Go2; offboard RTX 4090 desktop, Ethernet and motion capture.
architecture: Sampling-based receding-horizon control; direct torque output.
verification: Full text: Fig. 7, conclusion and Appendix A checked; preprint 2024 / ICRA 2025.

title: DiffuseLoco: Real-Time Legged Locomotion Control with Diffusion from Offline Datasets
overview: Learns a multi-skill locomotion policy from offline data, using a receding action horizon.
achievement: Reports real quadruped deployment, transitions between locomotion skills, and edge-device execution.
gap: This demonstrates locomotion-policy synthesis; it does not establish arbitrary precision flips or terrain-aware pronking sequences. Dataset coverage and action-generation latency remain relevant.
setting: Quadruped physical locomotion demonstrations; controlled evaluations.
order: No explicit online dynamics optimizer; data-driven action policy.
architecture: Offline diffusion policy with receding-horizon execution.
verification: Author project and abstract checked; CoRL 2024.

title: Diffusion-based learning of contact plans for agile locomotion
overview: Search generates feasible contact plans; diffusion learns their multiple possible solutions and supplies a whole-body controller.
achievement: Simulated Solo12 selects contact sequences for jumping on sparse stepping stones.
gap: Hardware implementation remains future work in v5. Known terrain, restricted gait search and low success on a difficult changing-stone task limit generalization claims.
setting: Solo12 simulation; not a physical stepping-stone demonstration.
architecture: High-level diffusion contact planner + low-level NMPC.
verification: v5 full text, including conclusion, checked (23 June 2025). First preprint 2024 used a different title.

title: DynaFlow: Dynamics-embedded Flow Matching for Physically Consistent Motion Generation from State-only Demonstrations
overview: Maps generated actions through a differentiable simulator so learning can use state-only demonstrations.
achievement: Physical Go1 reproduces varied gaits and stylistic motions; the project reports long-horizon open-loop execution.
gap: Consistency is with the embedded model. It does not guarantee disturbance recovery in the real world or establish a closed-loop acrobatic pronking system.
architecture: Flow-matching action generation trained through a simulator.

title: Integrating Diffusion-based Multi-task Learning with Online Reinforcement Learning for Robust Quadruped Robot Control
overview: DMLoco combines offline multi-task diffusion training with reinforcement-learning refinement.
achievement: The abstract reports language-conditioned skills, more stable task transitions and onboard inference at 50 Hz.
gap: This is adjacent multi-skill locomotion evidence. The abstract alone does not establish acrobatic landing accuracy or unseen-terrain pronking reliability.
setting: Real-world deployment reported in abstract; detailed test setting not audited.
order: No explicit online physics planner described.
architecture: Diffusion pretraining + PPO in simulation + onboard policy.
verification: arXiv v2 abstract checked (September 2025); experimental tables not audited.

title: Quadruped Parkour Learning: Sparsely Gated Mixture of Experts with Visual Input
overview: A sparse expert network allocates computation conditionally inside a vision-based parkour policy.
achievement: On a 32 cm box, MoE succeeds in 10/10 trials versus 5/10 for an MLP with matched active parameters. Outdoor obstacle demonstrations are included.
gap: Small trial counts do not establish field reliability. Expert selection adds tuning. The reported speed comparison uses batch size 6000, not simply onboard latency.
setting: Go2 + D435f camera; policy runs offboard on RTX 2060.
order: Simulation-trained policy, no explicit online dynamics optimization.
architecture: Depth-conditioned RL with sparse MoE actor.
verification: Full text: Table III, hardware setup, outdoor tests and conclusion checked.

title: Behavior Foundations for Quadruped Robots: ABot-C0 Technical Report
overview: Transfers the large-data motion-tracking recipe prominent in humanoids to quadruped behavior learning.
achievement: Reports 16,074 feasible motion clips, a flow-matching motion-tracking policy, and real-world navigation / interaction experiments.
gap: Generalist tracking and urban navigation are not quantitative proof of arbitrary flips, precise repeated landings, or low-gravity performance. Independent replication is not assessed.
setting: Urban-terrain navigation and interaction; detailed experiment audit pending.
order: Data-driven tracking; underlying simulator order not audited.
architecture: Flow tracking + privileged-to-perceptive locomotion + multi-policy coordination.
verification: July 2026 arXiv v2 technical-report abstract checked; author claims, not independent replication.

title: SpaceBok: A Dynamic Legged Robot for Space Exploration
overview: A purpose-built quadruped uses leg geometry and parallel elasticity for powerful hopping.
achievement: The primary paper reports physical walking, trotting and pronking, with single jumps up to 1.05 m. Lunar-pronking predictions are simulated.
gap: Earth jumping does not establish operation in lunar dust, vacuum or thermal extremes. ETH describes the platform as not space-graded.
setting: Earth-based physical robot; simulated lunar locomotion.
order: Elastic mechanism and model-based control; order not audited.
verification: ETH-hosted paper and ETH platform description checked.
environment: Extraterrestrial motivation; hardware tests on Earth.

title: SpaceHopper: A Small-Scale Legged Robot for Exploring Low-Gravity Celestial Bodies
overview: A three-legged robot explores how moving limbs can orient the body during long low-gravity flights. This is related work, not a quadruped.
achievement: Physical tests use a rotational gimbal and counterweight setup. Six-metre commanded jumps are reported in simulated Ceres gravity (0.029 g).
gap: The simulated distance is not a hardware jump record. Gimbal and counterweight tests do not establish autonomous flight and landing on an asteroid.
setting: 5.2 kg three-legged robot; Earth gimbal / counterweight rigs.
environment: Asteroid / moon target; simulation and Earth-based tests.

title: DeepMimic: Example-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning of Physics-Based Character Skills
overview: A shared imitation-plus-task formulation learns diverse motions in simulated characters.
achievement: Demonstrates acrobatics, locomotion and recovery across simulated human, Atlas, dinosaur and dragon characters.
gap: A simulated Atlas character is not a physical Atlas experiment. This provides methodological ancestry, not evidence of quadruped-to-biped hardware policy transfer.
setting: Physics-based character animation; no physical hardware demonstration.
verification: Author project and primary paper checked.

title: Learning Agile Robotic Locomotion Skills by Imitating Animals
overview: Retargets animal motion references to learn robot skills, extending motion-imitation ideas to physical quadrupeds.
achievement: Reports physical quadruped locomotion, dynamic hops and turns from reference-guided learning.
gap: Reference availability, retargeting and simulator mismatch matter. It does not show that a humanoid controller can be copied unchanged onto a quadruped.
setting: Physical quadruped demonstrations after simulation training.
order: Articulated simulation; learned policy at deployment.
verification: Primary abstract and author project checked.

title: ASAP: Aligning Simulation and Real-World Physics for Learning Agile Humanoid Whole-Body Skills
overview: Uses real robot rollouts to learn an action correction inside the simulator, then fine-tunes the motion policy.
achievement: Unitree G1 hardware demonstrates agile human-like skills; author examples include forward and sideways jumps and a jump with rotation.
gap: Requires real-world data collection. This is a humanoid method with related ingredients, not demonstrated quadruped-to-humanoid acrobatic transfer.
setting: Unitree G1 physical demonstrations and simulator-transfer experiments.
order: Articulated simulation corrected by learned delta actions.
architecture: Two-stage motion imitation and sim-to-real fine-tuning.
verification: Author project and primary abstract checked; RSS 2025.

title: BeyondMimic: From Motion Tracking to Versatile Humanoid Control via Guided Diffusion
overview: First learn dynamic motion tracking, then distill selected motion policies into a guided diffusion policy.
achievement: The tracking pipeline demonstrates jumping spins and cartwheels; diffusion demonstrations include waypoint following, teleoperation and obstacle avoidance.
gap: Do not attribute every acrobatic tracker result to the unified diffusion controller. The project uses motion capture for some navigation / state-estimation demonstrations.
setting: Humanoid physical demonstrations; motion-capture-assisted downstream tests.
order: Articulated training simulation; distilled generative policy.
architecture: RL motion tracking + diffusion distillation + test-time guidance.
verification: Author project and 2025 preprint abstract checked; results separated by pipeline stage.
